I have been farming this wheat-maize rotation on my 9.8 mu for 25 years. My family has only three people, and some of us work off-farm, so I cannot waste labor. I know this land well. For wheat, I will rotary-till the soil after the maize harvest, sow my usual improved wheat seed, and apply one bag of compound fertilizer—about 50 kg per mu—because that is what the shop sells and what I have always used. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings survive the cold, once at jointing, and once at grain filling, using my well. I will spray insecticide twice when I see aphids or other pests. For summer maize, I do not till the soil after wheat harvest—I just sow directly to save time and diesel. I will plant hybrid seed, Denghai 605, because it gives me the best yield. I will apply 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, irrigate twice when it gets dry, and spray once for insects and once for weeds. I expect my wheat to yield around 600 kg per mu and my maize around 616 kg per mu, which is what I usually get if the weather is normal.
